title: Training Notes on Due-Day Changes, Automatic Payment and Hardship Skips
content:
Patient Services Academy — training notes on changing the schedule of a **Patient Payment Plans** plan. The rules are stated first; the questions after them are answered from those rules alone.

## The rules

- **Active plans only.** The schedule of a plan can be changed only while the plan status is active. A plan that is pending acceptance, past due, defaulted, paid off or cancelled cannot have its schedule changed.
- **Due day.** The due day may be changed at most the term's allowed number of times over the life of the plan, to a day between the term's earliest and latest due day. The change applies from the next installment not yet due. Once the plan's count of due-day changes has reached the allowance, no further change is made.
- **Automatic payment.** Automatic payment may be switched between the term's methods for automatic draws at any time, but cannot be turned off on a term that requires automatic payment.
- **Hardship skip.** A hardship skip defers one not-yet-due installment to after the last installment, extending the plan by one month. At most the term's allowance of skips is granted per plan, counting every installment deferred over the life of the plan, and only with a supporting document where the term requires one. A skip does not change the installment amount.

## Questions answered

**A patient on an active plan has already changed the due day once, on a term that allows one change. Can it be changed again?** No. The count has reached the allowance.

**A patient on a 24-Month Extended Payment Plan changed the due day once. Can it be changed a second time?** Yes, if the plan is active and the new day is within the allowed range; that term allows two changes.

**The patient asks to move the due day to the 30th.** The 30th is outside the range of due days every term allows.

**When does a new due day take effect?** From the next installment that is not yet due; installments already due keep their dates.

**Can a patient on an 18-Month Payment Plan stop automatic payments and pay manually?** No; that term requires automatic payment. The patient may switch to another of the term's methods for automatic draws.

**A plan is past due and the patient asks for a hardship skip.** The schedule cannot be changed on a past-due plan.

**What does a hardship skip do to the amount and the end date?** The deferred installment moves to after the last installment, the plan runs one month longer, and the installment amount stays the same.

**Can an installment that is already due be skipped?** No. A skip defers a not-yet-due installment.

## Skip allowance check (hypothetical active plans)

| Term allowance | Installments already deferred on the plan | Supporting document supplied (where required) | Skip may be granted |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1 | Yes | Yes |
| 2 | 2 | Yes | No |
| 1 | 0 | No, and the term requires one | No |
| 0 | 0 | Yes | No |
